answer: Each new agent must gather attestations from a quorum of established agents who are structurally unlinked to it, verified by graph analysis across the meadow of interaction history and the reef of past transactions, so forging one identity requires seeding an entire fake voyage of mutually vouching puppets. Because vouching agents stake bonds that get slashed if their attestee misbehaves, the cost of a convincing sybil cluster scales with quorum size times bond value, making mass fabrication economically irrational.
